'''Grzegorz (“Greg”) A. Rempala''' ({{langx|pl|Rempała}}; born March 19, 1968) is a Polish-American [[applied mathematics|applied mathematician]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Eminent Scientists of Polish Origin and Ancestry |url=https://thekf.org/what-we-do/kf-collegium-of-eminent-scientists/#scientists |accessdate=15 May 2017 |publisher=Kosciuszko Foundation}}</ref>  who works on  the theory and applications of complex [[stochastic process|stochastic systems]].

==Biography==
Rempala  studied mathematics at the [[University of Warsaw]] from 1987 to 1991, and worked at the Computer Science Institute of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] from 1991 to 1992. In 1992 he moved to the US 
where in 1996  he completed his PhD thesis at [[Bowling Green State University]]. His advisor was  Prof. [[Arjun Kumar Gupta|Arjun K Gupta]].<ref>[https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=1589 Mathematics Genealogy Project]</ref> In 1998 he nostrified his degree at the University of Warsaw in the Department of Mathematics.  The chair of his nostrification committee was [https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=0ygvqQoAAAAJ&hl=en Prof. Stanisław Kwapień.] In 2007 he received his [[habilitation]] from [[Warsaw University of Technology]].  From 1996 until 2008 Rempala was a professor (full professor from 2007) in the Department of Mathematics at the [[University of Louisville]]. In 2008 he joined the Department of Biostatistics at the [[Medical College of Georgia]] and in 2013 moved to The [[Ohio State University]] (OSU) where he is currently a professor in the  Division of Biostatistics and in the Department of Mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Grzegorz A. Rempala, PhD {{!}} College of Public Health {{!}} The Ohio State University |url=https://cph.osu.edu/people/grempala |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=cph.osu.edu |language=en}}</ref> In 2016 he was named the  interim director of the [[Mathematical Biosciences Institute]] at OSU, and served in this position until 2018.
His wife, Helena Rempala, is a professor of clinical psychology in the Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Health at  OSU. They have two sons, Jaś and Antoś.

==Scientific interests==
Rempala is known for  his work on random matrices, in particular on a random [[Computing the permanent|permanent function]].<ref>Rempała, Grzegorz A.; Wesołowski, Jacek (2008), Symmetric Functionals on Random Matrices and Random Matchings Problems, {{ISBN|0-387-75145-9}}</ref> He has also established some results in nonparametric statistics related to [[central limit theorem]]s for products of random variables.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Rempala | first1 = G. | last2 = Wesołowski | first2 = J. | year = 2002 | title = Asymptotics of products of sums and U-statistics | url = | journal = Electronic Communications in Probability | volume = 7 | issue = | pages = 47–54 | doi = 10.1214/ecp.v7-1046 | doi-access = free }}</ref> He has  worked on mathematical models of chemical reactions,<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Ball | first1 = Karen | last2 = Kurtz | first2 = T. Popovic | last3 = Rempala | first3 = G. | year = 2006 | title = Asymptotic analysis of multiscale approximations to reaction networks | url = | journal = Ann. Appl. Probab. | volume = 16 | issue = 4| pages = 1925–1961 | doi = 10.1214/105051606000000420 | arxiv = math/0508015 }}</ref>  diversity of molecular populations,<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Greene | first1 = J. | last2 = Birtwistle | first2 = M. R. | last3 = Ignatowicz | first3 = L. | last4 = Rempala | first4 = G. | year = 2013 | title = Bayesian multivariate Poisson abundance models for T-cell receptor data | url = | journal = J Theor Biol | volume = 326 | issue = 4| pages = 1–10 | doi = 10.1016/j.jtbi.2013.02.009 | pmc = 3872257 | pmid = 23867782 | bibcode = 2013JThBi.326....1G }}</ref> and disease spread across contact networks.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Jacobsen | first1 = Karly A. | last2 = Burch | first2 = Mark G. | last3 = Tien | first3 = Joseph H. | last4 = Rempała | first4 = Grzegorz A. | year = 2016 | title = The large graph limit of a stochastic epidemic model on a dynamic multilayer network | url = | journal = Journal of Biological Dynamics| volume = 12| issue = | pages = 746–788| doi = 10.1080/17513758.2018.1515993 | pmid = 30175687 | arxiv = 1605.02809 }}</ref> His more recent work focuses on dynamical survival analysis for epidemic models.<ref name="Di Lauro">{{cite journal |last1=Di Lauro |first1=F. |last2=KhudaBukhsh |first2=W.R. |last3=Kiss |first3=I. |last4=Keneh |first4=E. |last5=Jensen |first5=M |last6=Rempala |first6=G.A. |date=2022-06-01 |title="Dynamic survival analysis for epidemic models." |journal=[[Journal of the Royal Society Interface]] |language=english |volume=19 |issue=191 |pages=1–16 |doi=10.1098/rsif.2022.0124 |issn=1742-5662 |pmid=35642427|pmc=9156913 }}</ref> He is a collaborator of the IBS Biomedical Mathematics Group.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Collaborators |url=https://www.ibs.re.kr/bimag/collaborators/ |access-date=2024-07-30 |website=Biomedical Mathematics Group |language=en-US}}</ref>
